exceptions.reason: The probe polls, under a 30 s ceiling, until the Agent's aux worker thread exists; nothing announces that thread, so the sleep is the poll interval.
The test polls, under a 60 s ceiling, for the guard run that chat.refine's background review records, then asserts the count; the sleep is the poll interval.
_wait_until is the file's one ceiling-bounded poll for what another process decides (the worker's pid file, a grandchild's exit); the sleep is its poll interval.
_wait_for_file polls, under a 60 s ceiling, for the ready file a real cron script child writes; the sleep is its poll interval.
wait_for is the file's ceiling-bounded poll helper, and the fixture gateway's hold_terminal polls for the release file the test touches; both sleeps are poll intervals across processes.
The fake cron children simulate a slow cooperative exit and an unresponsive worker for the parent's settlement code under test.
The paused Agent writer polls for the test's go file and wait_for_mark polls for a child's mark file, both under a 30 s ceiling; the sleeps are poll intervals across processes.

The probe backdates a seeded ledger row against the Agent's wall clock, past its 60 s orphan threshold but inside its 300 s claim lease, which the sweep reads from time.time(); it measures no elapsed time.
_drain_until polls process.drain, the owner's record, under a 15 s ceiling until the exited process's completion appears; the sleep is its poll interval.
The test polls, under a 5 s ceiling, until three followers wait on the in-flight walk's condition, which signals no waiter; the sleep is the poll interval.
_streaming polls the captured RPC output, under a 10 s ceiling, for the stream's ready event; the sleep is the poll interval.
_wait_parked polls the Agent's parked approvals under a 20 s ceiling inside the probe's Agent interpreter; the sleep is the poll interval.
settled polls, under a 3 s ceiling inside the probe's Agent interpreter, for the interrupt the Agent's off-thread bg-review-cancel delivers to the fork; the sleep is the poll interval.
wait_for is the file's ceiling-bounded poll for what the sidecar and its synthetic Agent processes record (marker files, pause records, process_snapshot rows); the sleep is its poll interval.

The synthetic native-Agent double's gateway writer, lock release gate, resume readiness check, fsmonitor mutator and hung git apply simulate running, gated or wedged Agent processes for the mutation owner under test.
Stand-in serve and gateway children the probes resolve identities of: one idles until the probe terminates it, the other until the probe touches its exit marker.

The synthetic service manager, supervisor and gateway writer simulate launchd/systemd services for the custody code under test: their main loop, the hold gates the tests open, and their ceiling-bounded readiness, stop and successor waits poll every 10 ms.
The test polls, under a 15 s ceiling, for the archived.json the profile plugin's hook writes inside the sidecar process; the sleep is the poll interval.

The synthetic dependency-sync writer and its grandchild keep writing to simulate a running venv sync for the RPC owner's reaping, and _wait is the file's ceiling-bounded poll for their pid files and exit; the sleeps are their pacing and poll interval.
The synthetic venv_sync writer loops until the cancelled recovery reaps it, simulating a running dependency writer for the recovery owner's child cleanup under test.
The peer fixture polls, under a 5 s ceiling, until the peer's serve_forever thread has taken the RPC channel, which nothing announces; the sleep is the poll interval.
wait_for and the post-abort liveness check are the test's ceiling-bounded polls for a worker's pid file and a reaped child's exit; the sleeps are poll intervals.

Synthetic test and wrapper files the runner executes poll, under ceilings, for markers sibling workers or the test write (overlap barriers, the abort gate, child startup, orphan reaping); the sleeps are poll intervals.
Stand-in long-lived children and tests that hold a worker busy until the runner aborts it, its leak fixture kills them, or the test releases them.
The pool test's synthetic cases hold their active marker briefly so a third concurrent worker, which the bounded pool must never start, would see it.
Three are the session-open probe's ceilings on its bounded polls and one is a turn duration printed only in failure messages; no assertion compares elapsed time to an expected value.
Phase timings the real-owner peers print as PHASES diagnostics; no test asserts on them.
Backdates the fixture worktree's mtimes two days past the Agent's 24-hour sweep threshold; nothing is measured.
Poll interval inside the leak guard's 30 s ceiling-bounded wait, read from process_snapshot, for the Agent's detached scratch prune to exit.
Poll interval inside the probe's 20 s ceiling-bounded wait for the parked approval.
Poll intervals inside the peer's 45 s and 60 s ceiling-bounded waits on the owner's snapshot and its workers' exit.
Poll intervals inside the probes' ceiling-bounded waits on the owner's snapshot, prompts, opens log and state.db admissions.
The synthetic on_session_open plugin holds a delivery past the owner's OPEN_TURN_WAIT_S bound: the slow consumer the probe proves a Web turn never waits on.
Poll intervals inside the group probe's 40 s and 60 s ceiling-bounded waits on the room's state and log.
Poll interval inside the probe's settle helper, bounded by its 20 s CEILING.
Poll intervals inside the _cancels and _ended helpers' ceiling-bounded waits for events recorded on release threads.
Poll intervals inside 20 s ceiling-bounded waits for the connect operation to settle.
The synthetic hung gateway child outlives the restart's background wait, so the code under test must time it out and terminate it.
Poll intervals inside the settle and wait_until helpers' ceiling-bounded waits on the flow's state.
Poll interval inside the until helper's 60 s ceiling-bounded wait on the flow's state.
Poll interval inside the sidecar script's 10 s ceiling-bounded wait for the device login to end.
The synthetic wedged tool ignores its interrupt and polls for the test's release flag under a 120 s ceiling.

The config.get fake answers after 50 ms to stand in for a real RPC; app.ts awaits the profile config read for every /api/ request before its gates, so the test passes at any delay (checked at 1 ms and 500 ms) and fails once that await is removed.

The settleCommand fake answers after 150 ms to stand in for a slow record write; turn.ts awaits opts.onDone before it publishes stream_end, so the test passes at any delay (checked at 1 ms and 500 ms) and fails once that await is removed.

The chat.evict_agent fake answers after 20 ms to stand in for a slow sidecar; service.ts awaits the eviction before it finalizes the compression, so the test passes at any delay (checked at 1 ms and 500 ms) and fails once that await is removed.
testPlainTextStillPastesIntoTitleAndDetails proves UIKit's own paste(_:), which reads only the general pasteboard, so it saves, writes and restores that pasteboard.
activateSend(in:) is the one helper that activates Send, after waiting until it reports enabled.
attachWindowImage draws a window only for an attachment someone keeps: a failed test's screenshot, or a TALARIA_TEST_SCREENSHOTS run.
blockUntilRequestsFinish polls URLSession.allTasks under a 10 s ceiling from a detached task while the main actor stays blocked; URLSession announces no idle state, so the sleep is the poll interval.
connectionFast replaces the operation's real 2 s read interval with 5 ms, so a test watches the read loop run until the server settles the operation.
PollingLoopHold gives the clarification loop a 1 ms interval until its stream fails and it starts reading HTTP, then parks it; the interval is the fake's stand-in for the real 1.5 s one.

makeState hands the board the real sleep with 5 ms coalescing and reconnect delays, and PollingIntervalHold passes those delays through and lets the first polling interval elapse before it parks the loop; tests wait on the board's effects, never on these durations.
The stub protocol spaces its SSE chunks by each chunk's delay to simulate a network that delivers a stream in pieces.

The suites' shared helpers: pollUntil's poll interval under its 10 s ceiling, parkUntilCancelled's stand-in for a reply that never comes, HeldRoundTrips' poll that groups requests starting together (nothing announces a round trip's end), and MockAuthAPIClient's optional authStatusDelay latency fake.
The watchdog's own test hands it work that deliberately outlives its 0.2 s budget, to prove the hang detector reports it.

The native-drag variants, run only by scripts/test-history-drag, sample committed frames for 3 s while an external driver moves the simulator's real touch; no in-process event marks the end of that gesture.

awaitElement, awaitCondition and composerTextView are the hosted suites' shared waits; each polls the screen every 50 ms under its 10 s ceiling, since a hosted screen announces no change to its accessibility tree or text views.
The typing helper's own tests simulate the loads it must survive: an editor that mounts 2.4 s late and a main actor blocked for 10.5 s, past the helper's former ceiling.
A repeating timer blocks the main run loop for 10 ms at a time to simulate a busy runner, so an immediate archive response lands between SwiftUI frames.
